brief: A wall-hung spice rack: at least three bins, hung from keyhole hangers.

requirements.evidence: Three hex-acc-keyhole hangers on slot 2 (the same back face) of each base. The configurator checks fit only, so whether the wall screws and the plastic can carry the full rack's weight can't be checked here.

requirements.requirement: Works as a wall-hung spice rack, with spice jars shown in the bins
requirements.evidence: The bins and hangers make the rack, but the catalogue has no spice jar prop. I put glass tumblers in the three bins as stand-ins, and they show in the view.

finish.summary: I built a wall-hung spice rack from three hex bases in a row, each holding a half-depth bin. A keyhole hanger sits on the same back face of each base, so the rack lifts onto screws already in the wall. The open faces are capped and the joints between bases are bolted. The configurator's checks pass and the meshes clear each other. The prop catalogue has no spice jars, so I used glass tumblers as stand-ins, one in each bin. The parts are 20 lines and the print estimate is about 1417 g.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
